**Question 1**: Why does the callback of the listener get called? If my understanding is correct - spin is only required for the subscription (+ timers + services) part of the communication; the publishing is independent of that, right?


And back to my original problem (that I wanted to describe in my first comment). Suppose you modify the following files like you suggested:

publisher.cpp
```
#include "demo/publisher.hpp"

#include <chrono>

using namespace std::chrono_literals;

namespace demo {
Publisher::Publisher() : Node("publisher") {
    this->pub_ = this->create_publisher<std_msgs::msg::Float64>("comm_topic");

    this->timer_ = this->create_wall_timer(1ms, [this]() {
        std_msgs::msg::Float64 msg;
        msg.data = this->counter_;
        RCLCPP_INFO(this->get_logger(), "Publishing %f", this->counter_);
        this->pub_->publish(msg);
        this->counter_ += 0.01;
    });
}

Publisher::~Publisher() {

}
}
```

publisher.hpp
```
#ifndef DEMO__PUBLISHER_HPP_
#define DEMO__PUBLISHER_HPP_

#include "rclcpp/rclcpp.hpp"

#include "std_msgs/msg/float64.hpp"

#include "demo/visibility_control.h"

namespace demo {

    class Publisher : public rclcpp::Node {
    public:
        explicit Publisher();

        virtual ~Publisher();
    private:
        rclcpp::Publisher<std_msgs::msg::Float64>::SharedPtr pub_;
        rclcpp::TimerBase::SharedPtr timer_;

        double counter_;
    };

}  // namespace demo

#endif  // DEMO__PUBLISHER_HPP_
```

publisher_node.cpp
```
#include <memory>
#include <thread>
#include <chrono>

#include "rclcpp/rclcpp.hpp"

#include "demo/publisher.hpp"

int main(int argc, char ** argv)
{
    setvbuf(stdout, nullptr, _IONBF, BUFSIZ);

    printf("Initialize communications\n");
    rclcpp::init(argc, argv);
    printf("Initialize communications - done\n");

    printf("Create node\n");
    auto node = std::make_shared<demo::Publisher>();
    printf("Create node - done\n");

    printf("Sleeping\n");
    std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(1000));
    printf("Sleeping - done\n");

    printf("Spin\n");
    rclcpp::spin(node);
    printf("Spin - done\n");

    printf("Shutdown\n");
    rclcpp::shutdown();
    printf("Shutdown - done\n");

    return 0;
}
```

This behavior is really awkward in my opinion. The listener just stops. I would have expected that it either drops messages (if it can't process them fast enough).

**Question 2**:  Is this a bug (known)? Can we somehow get information from the listener that something like this happened? With smaller frequencies (10Hz), this problem didn't happen on my machine.

> Question 1: Why does the callback of the listener get called? If my understanding is correct - spin is only required for the subscription (+ timers + services) part of the communication; the publishing is independent of that, right?

I don't think spinning is required for publishers. AFAIK, we only need to spin for entities where we're waiting for something to be executed (e.g. a callback).

> Question 2: Is this a bug (known)? Can we somehow get information from the listener that something like this happened? With smaller frequencies (10Hz), this problem didn't happen on my machine.

It sounds like a bug. I'm unable to reproduce on Linux (Ubuntu 18.04); all messages appear to make it to the subscriber. Perhaps it is related to Windows. I'll try next time I'm at a Windows machine.

Can you confirm if the same issue happens with `std_msgs::msg::String`? (i.e. just change the [update rate in the demo talker](https://github.com/ros2/demos/blob/df5ec3a477c683bbaf9b3a2ec064680a0d36829d/demo_nodes_cpp/src/topics/talker.cpp#L63)).

> It sounds like a bug. I'm unable to reproduce on Linux (Ubuntu 18.04); all messages appear to make it to the subscriber. Perhaps it is related to Windows. I'll try next time I'm at a Windows machine.

I have been able to reproduce it on Linux (after retrying a bunch of times). The worst case I have seen:
our demos with the timer changed to 100us, published up to message number 4700, listened up to message 4676.

> I don't think spinning is required for publishers. AFAIK, we only need to spin for entities where we're waiting for something to be executed (e.g. a callback).

I suppose that spinning isn't needed for publishers, but I'm not sure.
The same problem happens with the demo talker/listener (so with String messages) if I change the rate.
This problem seems to be related to Fast-RTPS. Using OpenSplice for DDS implementation, I can't reproduce this problem unlike Fast-RTPS.

> This problem seems to be related to Fast-RTPS. Using OpenSplice for DDS implementation, I can't reproduce this problem unlike Fast-RTPS.

Good catch.
I have seen a difference of one message after `cntrl+c`-ing in `opensplice` (and I moved the log after the `publish` in the talker code). But in `fastrtps` the problem seems to be much worst.
